newsitem.title: SPAIN: Labour reform cuts into Spain unemployment - Lab Min.
newsitem.headline: Labour reform cuts into Spain unemployment - Lab Min.

text.p: The Spanish Labour Ministry said on Monday that 4,948 employment contracts were agreed last month under the new labour reform act which took effect on May 17.
Of these, 2,668 were conversions to permanent from former temporary contracts, while 1,022 were new training contracts and 1,258 were permanent contracts, the ministry said in a statement.

Labour reform, agreed between union and employers' associations, was an attempt to reduce the fragility of job contracts in the Spanish market, reduce the cost of dismissals and promote jobs for young persons.
In May, unemployment fell by 57,866 to 13.26 percent, the Labour Ministry said.
